# Tables

Open **Window → Editors → Tables** to enter project-wide Csound function
table statements. Blue saves this text with the project and puts it at the
start of `<CsScore>`, ahead of [Global Score](globals.qmd) text and notes
generated from the timeline.

For example, this statement creates a sine-wave table numbered `1`:

```csound-sco
f1 0 4096 10 1
```

An instrument can then refer to table `1` in its Csound code. Give each
manually numbered table a number that does not conflict with another table
in the project. When choosing numbers for tables generated by instruments and
SoundObjects, Blue reserves numeric `f` numbers from this editor and numeric
`ftgen` numbers it finds in Global Orchestra text. It cannot infer numbers
supplied indirectly through variables or macros. It does not reserve table
numbers written in Global Score or instrument score text, so those can conflict
with automatically generated tables. Check the generated CSD when you define
tables in those locations. The Tables editor stores score text directly; it
does not place a SoundObject on the timeline or change the Score's visible
duration.

Use **Project → Generate CSD to Screen** to confirm the table statement and
the instrument that reads it. See [Orchestra](orchestra.qmd) for instrument
editing and [Global Orchestra and Global Score](globals.qmd) for other
project-wide Csound text.
